name: spellkave_orient
label: Spellkave Orient
description: Rebuild your situation from the world in one call: self/scene/in-world turn-scene/manipulation and sensing facts plus inventory and the MOST RECENT page of traces — the one thing an actor with no history legitimately needs (a fresh conversation, a reloaded world, a restarted host). Freely callable mid-run too, as a situation refresh. Traces are bounded and page most-recent-first, never the whole history at once; pass the returned traces.next_cursor back as cursor to go further back, one page per call. view.manipulation_context uses the same snake_case rows as spellkave_manipulation_context (a prompts[] row from either is the same semantic_context); its actions are bounded to the most relevant rows (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical) with actions_total, actions_more and actions_by_niche saying what was left out — call spellkave_manipulation_context for more_action_ids (every other action id) and pass action_ids there for the syntax rows of named actions.

cursor.description: Opaque traces.next_cursor from a prior spellkave_orient call — fetches the NEXT (older) page of traces. Omit for the first call: the most recent page, which stands alone as a usable orientation.

limit.description: Traces per page (default 10, max 25). Going further back costs more calls, deliberately — recall should cost turns, not one unbounded dump.

argumentGates: Caller-owned acting context only; presence is nonspatial and conveys no NPC consent.
